title: False-Consensus Effect
coreMove: Name the false consensus effect in the room, then redesign the next choice so it cannot choose for you.
sourcePressure: The frozen TOC and official source notes frame False-Consensus Effect as a specific decision error around false consensus, projection, survey. Traceable support includes The False Consensus Effect: An egocentric bias in social perception and attribution processes.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating False-Consensus Effect as generic advice to be smarter, instead of forcing this exact move: name the false consensus effect in the room, then redesign the next choice so it cannot choose for you.

hook: Do not open with a definition of False-Consensus Effect.
Do not use a generic panic-at-a-meeting opener.
counterintuition: Avoid the reusable shape where the obvious answer is wrong and the opposite is true.
Do not make False-Consensus Effect sound like ordinary carelessness.
examples: No coffee mug, classroom whiteboard, bus depot, radiator, bike helmet, or narrow kitchen shell.
No example may skip the specific mechanics of False-Consensus Effect.
